questions.question: Why is it good to keep space between you and other vehicles?

options.text: You can draft off of other vehicles.
You have more time to react to what other drivers do.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to react to what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your motorcycle at all times. If something happens, you will have more time to respond and more room to move safely.

questions.question: If bright sunlight hides your turn signals, you should:

options.text: Keep using your mechanical turn signals.
Honk your horn to tell other drivers you are turning.

questions.explanation: Use hand signals when bright sunlight makes your turn signals hard to see. It is very important to tell other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder.
Check your mirrors. You only need to look over your shoulder if something seems wrong.
Either check your mirrors or look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, make sure no one is in your path. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.question: Why should you not rely only on your mirrors?

options.text: Mirrors can get dirty and block your view.

questions.explanation: You need to know what is around you. Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles.

questions.question: To help others see your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.explanation: Using your headlight is the best way to help others see your motorcycle. Always check that your headlight works before you ride.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT greatly affect your blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.explanation: The main factors that affect BAC are how much you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight.

questions.question: What about blind spots on motorcycles?

options.text: They do not exist if the motorcycle has a rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Make this a routine habit.

questions.question: When riding near a truck, remember:

options.text: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
You should not be able to see the truck's mirrors.
You should focus on riding and not worry about the truck's mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Avoid staying in the blind spots of large trucks. Remember: if you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: When being passed, moving to the far side of your lane:

options.text: Is a good idea because you will be farther from the passing vehicle.
Is not a good idea because it may cause the other driver to move back too soon.
Does not affect safety either way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not a good idea because it may cause the other driver to move back too soon.
questions.explanation: When being passed, do not move to the far side of your lane. This may cause the passing driver to move back into your lane too early.

questions.question: When braking on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. If you only use the rear brake, you will not develop the skill to use the front brake when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: Experienced riders use "SIPDE" to stay aware of their surroundings. What does the "D" stand for?
questions.explanation: SIPDE is a five-step process riders use to make decisions and take action while riding. The letters stand for Scan, Identify, Predict, Decide, and Execute.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to:
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to drift into another lane or leave the road. Always slow down before entering a turn or curve.

questions.question: When towing a trailer on a motorcycle, the following distance should:
questions.explanation: When towing a trailer, increase your following distance. The extra weight means your motorcycle needs more time to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely, then proceed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then proceed when safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are stop signs. Come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: When the lights on this sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with flashing lights, stop completely and wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a potential problem?

options.text: Conditions that stay the same as you approach

questions.correctAnswerText: Conditions that stay the same as you approach
questions.explanation: Look ahead for potential problems on the roadway and make a plan to handle them safely.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, a motorcycle takes:

options.text: Less time to stop and speed up.
The same time to stop and speed up.
More time to stop and speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: More time to stop and speed up.
questions.explanation: Extra weight slows a motorcycle's acceleration and stopping. Your bike will respond more slowly with a passenger than when riding alone.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should NOT:

options.text: Choose a lane position that makes them visible.
Cover the clutch and brakes to reduce reaction time.

questions.explanation: At an intersection, position yourself to be visible, cover your clutch and brakes, and slow down. Avoid sudden speed or position changes, as other drivers may misunderstand your intentions.

questions.question: What can remove alcohol from a person's system?
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Nothing else speeds up this process.

questions.question: Most motorcycle and car accidents happen:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle and car collisions happen at intersections. The main cause is drivers failing to give the motorcycle the right-of-way.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the road with flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to move.
Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle stopped with flashing lights, you must change lanes to give it space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign tells you that traffic will merge ahead.

questions.question: Before riding, check your motorcycle clutch. It should feel:
questions.explanation: Check your clutch and throttle before riding. The throttle should snap back when released. The clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: Your front tire is flat. Your steering will suddenly feel:
questions.explanation: If steering suddenly feels heavy, your front tire may be flat. Stop and check your tires right away.

questions.question: Who must wear a helmet on a moving motorcycle?
questions.explanation: All riders and passengers must wear a helmet when riding a motorcycle, motor-driven cycle, or motorized bicycle.
